Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:193389
Court No. - 66

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 44142 of 2024
Applicant :- Jitendra Singh

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Jaichandra Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Sri Kuldeep Kumar Shukla, Advocate filed his power on behalf of the informant which is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri R.K. Pandey, Advocate holding brief of Sri Jaichandra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant; Shri K.K. Shukla, learned counsel for the informant and Sri Imran Khan, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
3.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
108 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC & Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Kishanpur,
District Fatehpur, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged on 22.5.2024 under section 306 IPC against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the daughter of the informant about one and half years before and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured her and pressurized her for divorce and due to their torture, his daughter on 18.5.2024 at about 5 am in the morning committed suicide by hanging herself.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that as there was no allegation of demand of dowry Jitendra Singh vs State Of U.P. on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141624178/
1 in the FIR, therefore, FIR of the present case was lodged under section 306 IPC but during investigation when the statement of the informant was recorded then he started making allegation of demand of dowry and torture and thereafter case was converted under section 304B IPC and therefore, it appears subsequently during investigation he developed the case and actually it is not a case of dowry death.
6. He further submitted that actually applicant who is husband of the deceased, was doing job in District Surat in the State of Gujarat and resided over there and deceased i.e. his wife always insisted to live with him in Surat but due to week financial condition he was unable to live with her in Gujarat and only due to this reason, she committed suicide by hanging herself.
7.

sentences.text: He further submitted that even post mortem report also suggests that deceased died due to hanging.

8. He further submitted that immediately after the incident, informant was informed and on the same day i.e. on 18.5.2024 he arrived and in his presence inquest was conducted and in the inquest he was one of the inquest witnesses and at that time he did not raise any objection but after four days, he lodged the FIR of the present case and this fact suggests that on the basis of false allegation,
applicant has been made accused in the present matter.
9.
He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 16.6.2024 i.e. for last six months.

10. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within one and half years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances but they could not dispute the fact that there was no allegation of demand of dowry in the FIR and FIR of the present case was lodged under section 306 IPC.
11.
They further could not dispute the fact that informant of the case was one of the inquest witness but FIR of the present case was lodged after four days.
12. They further could not dispute the fact that as per post mortem report, deceased died due to hanging.
13. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

14. However, it reflects that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within one and half years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances but as there no allegation of demand of dowry and torture in the FIR and FIR was lodged under section 306 IPC but subsequently when informant during investigation started making allegation of demand of dowry then case was converted under section 304 B IPC therefore, considering this fact, argument advanced by learned counsel for the applicant that subsequently it appears, informant developed the case and actually it is not a case of dowry death, cannot be completely brushed aside, at this stage.

sentences.text:
Further, from the post mortem report it appears, deceased died due to hanging and therefore,
prima facie, it appears to be a case of suicidal death and reason of suicide given by the learned counsel for the applicant, cannot be completely ruled out at this stage.

16. Further, from the record it also reflects, at the time of inquest informant was present and he was one of the inquest witnesses but inspite of that he lodged the FIR of the present case after four days.
17. Further, applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 16.6.2024.

18. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
19. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

20. Let the applicant-Jitendra Singh, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
21. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

22. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
